GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

NATIONAL BULLETIN NO. 73 (FINAL PRE-LANDFALL ADVISORY)
CYCLONIC STORM "AMBAR" OVER NORTHWEST BAY OF BENGAL

ISSUED AT 1300 HOURS IST ON WEDNESDAY, 14 OCTOBER 2026

1. **SYNOPSIS OF CURRENT STATUS**

The Very Severe Cyclonic Storm (VSCS) "AMBAR" over northwest Bay of Bengal moved north-northeastwards with a speed of about 14 kmph during the past six hours and lay centred at 1230 hours IST of today, the 14 October 2026, over northwest Bay of Bengal near latitude 20.4°N and longitude 86.4°E, about 60 km southeast of Paradip (Odisha), 80 km south-southeast of Kendrapara, and 110 km east-southeast of Bhubaneswar.

The system is likely to intensify slightly during the next six hours and cross Odisha coast close to south of Paradip between 1600 and 1800 hours IST of today, the 14 October 2026, as a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm with a maximum sustained wind speed of 140-150 kmph gusting to 165 kmph.

2. **LANDFALL DETAILS AS PER LATEST TRACK**

Based on the latest observations from the Doppler Weather Radar at Paradip, satellite imagery from INSAT-3DR, and ship/coastal buoy reports, the estimated point and time of landfall are as follows:

| Parameter | Latest Estimate |
| :--- | :--- |
| Likely Landfall Location | Close to south of Paradip, Odisha |
| Likely Landfall Date | 14 October 2026 |
| Likely Landfall Time Window | 1600 to 1800 hours IST |
| Forward Speed | 14 kmph (north-northeastwards) |

The IMD bulletin recorded that Cyclone Ambar's landfall_date was 2026-10-14. Record status: historical.

3. **WIND WARNING & COASTAL HAZARDS**

- **Gale wind speed reaching 140-150 kmph gusting to 165 kmph** is very likely to commence over coastal districts of Odisha from around 1400 hours IST of today.
- Wind speed reaching **100-110 kmph gusting to 125 kmph** is very likely over Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara, Bhadrak, and Balasore districts during the next 12 hours.
- Wind speed reaching **70-80 kmph gusting to 95 kmph** is likely over Khordha, Puri, Cuttack, and Jajpur districts.
- Storm surge of about **2.0 to 2.5 meters** above astronomical tide is likely to inundate low-lying areas of coastal districts of Jagatsinghpur and Kendrapara during the time of landfall.

4. **RAINFALL WARNING (ISOLATED TO SCATTERED)**

- **Extremely heavy rainfall (≥ 20 cm)** at isolated places very likely over Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara, Bhadrak, and Balasore districts of Odisha during 14-15 October.
- **Very heavy rainfall (12-20 cm)** at a few places very likely over Cuttack, Jajpur, Khordha, Puri, and Mayurbhanj districts.
- **Heavy to very heavy rainfall** at isolated places very likely over the remaining coastal districts of Odisha and adjoining districts of north coastal Andhra Pradesh.

5. **FISHERMEN WARNING**

- Fishermen are advised **not to venture into north Bay of Bengal and along & off Odisha coast** during 14-15 October.
- Fishermen out at sea are advised to return to the coast immediately.

6. **IMPACT ON EVACUATION & COORDINATION**

The Department has been issuing six-hourly advisories since 10 October 2026. The last bulletin before landfall (No. 72) was issued at 0700 hours IST today. This bulletin (No. 73) is the final pre-landfall advisory.

The Odisha State Disaster Management Authority (OSDMA) and the District Emergency Operation Centres (DEOCs) of Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara, Bhadrak, and Balasore have been kept informed of the latest track and intensity. The concerned authorities are advised to complete evacuation of people from vulnerable low-lying areas and ensure that all shelters are ready for occupancy by 1500 hours IST.

7. **NEXT BULLETIN**

The next bulletin (No. 74) will be issued at **1900 hours IST on 14 October 2026** after the system crosses the coast and will contain the landfall confirmation and post-landfall outlook.
**GOVERNMENT OF INDIA  
MINISTRY OF EARTH SCIENCES  
INDIA METEOROLOGICAL DEPARTMENT  
NEW DELHI**

According to the IMD bulletin, Cyclone Ambar's landfall_location was Puri coast. Record status: historical. At the time of landfall, the system was a **Cyclonic Storm** with estimated maximum sustained wind speed of **85-95 kmph gusting to 105 kmph** over the coastal districts of Odisha. The centre of the cyclone was located near latitude **19.8°N** and longitude **85.9°E** at 1700 hours IST.

The landfall occurred during high tide, and the associated storm surge of about 2.0 to 2.5 meters above astronomical tide inundated low-lying areas of Jagatsinghpur and Kendrapara districts as previously warned.

**2. CURRENT STATUS AND POST-LANDFALL TRACK**

The system has now weakened slightly and moved inland. At 1830 hours IST today, the cyclonic storm “Ambar” was centred near latitude **20.2°N** and longitude **85.4°E**, about 25 km north-northwest of Puri and 45 km south-southwest of Bhubaneswar.

The system is very likely to move north-northeastwards and weaken gradually into a **Deep Depression** during the next 6 hours, and into a **Depression** over north Odisha by tomorrow morning (15th October 2026).

The Very Severe Cyclonic Storm (VSCS) "AMBAR" over northwest Bay of Bengal moved north-northeastwards with a speed of about 14 kmph during the past six hours and lay centred at 1230 hours IST of today, the 14 October 2026, over northwest Bay of Bengal near latitude 20.4°N and longitude 86.4°E, about 60 km southeast of Paradip (Odisha), 80 km south-southeast of Kendrapara, and 110 km east-southeast of Bhubaneswar.

The system is likely to intensify slightly during the next six hours and cross Odisha coast close to south of Paradip between 1600 and 1800 hours IST of today, the 14 October 2026, as a Very Severe Cyclonic Storm with a maximum sustained wind speed of 140-150 kmph gusting to 165 kmph.

2. **LANDFALL DETAILS AS PER LATEST TRACK**

Based on the latest observations from the Doppler Weather Radar at Paradip, satellite imagery from INSAT-3DR, and ship/coastal buoy reports, the estimated point and time of landfall are as follows:

| Parameter | Latest Estimate |
| :--- | :--- |
| Likely Landfall Location | Close to south of Paradip, Odisha |
| Likely Landfall Date | 14 October 2026 |
| Likely Landfall Time Window | 1600 to 1800 hours IST |
| Forward Speed | 14 kmph (north-northeastwards) |

The IMD bulletin recorded that Cyclone Ambar's landfall_date was 2026-10-14. Record status: historical.

3. **WIND WARNING & COASTAL HAZARDS**

- **Gale wind speed reaching 140-150 kmph gusting to 165 kmph** is very likely to commence over coastal districts of Odisha from around 1400 hours IST of today.
- Wind speed reaching **100-110 kmph gusting to 125 kmph** is very likely over Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara, Bhadrak, and Balasore districts during the next 12 hours.
- Wind speed reaching **70-80 kmph gusting to 95 kmph** is likely over Khordha, Puri, Cuttack, and Jajpur districts.
- Storm surge of about **2.0 to 2.5 meters** above astronomical tide is likely to inundate low-lying areas of coastal districts of Jagatsinghpur and Kendrapara during the time of landfall.

4. **RAINFALL WARNING (ISOLATED TO SCATTERED)**

- **Extremely heavy rainfall (≥ 20 cm)** at isolated places very likely over Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara, Bhadrak, and Balasore districts of Odisha during 14-15 October.
- **Very heavy rainfall (12-20 cm)** at a few places very likely over Cuttack, Jajpur, Khordha, Puri, and Mayurbhanj districts.
- **Heavy to very heavy rainfall** at isolated places very likely over the remaining coastal districts of Odisha and adjoining districts of north coastal Andhra Pradesh.

5. **FISHERMEN WARNING**

- Fishermen are advised **not to venture into north Bay of Bengal and along & off Odisha coast** during 14-15 October.
- Fishermen out at sea are advised to return to the coast immediately.

6. **IMPACT ON EVACUATION & COORDINATION**

The Department has been issuing six-hourly advisories since 10 October 2026. The last bulletin before landfall (No. 72) was issued at 0700 hours IST today. This bulletin (No. 73) is the final pre-landfall advisory.

The Odisha State Disaster Management Authority (OSDMA) and the District Emergency Operation Centres (DEOCs) of Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapara, Bhadrak, and Balasore have been kept informed of the latest track and intensity. The concerned authorities are advised to complete evacuation of people from vulnerable low-lying areas and ensure that all shelters are ready for occupancy by 1500 hours IST.
